post.description:
The assistant's `reply` and the `conversation_id` to continue with.

The assistant is read-only: it sees a redacted, size-capped view of the next 7 days (and,
only if the user opted in, recent history and notes), and has no tools, so nothing it says
changes anything. Conversations are kept in memory (20 turns) and lost on restart: an unknown
`conversation_id` is a 404. Loopback only: a paired phone gets 403. At most 10 messages a
minute. 404 while chat is off (the default).

404.description: Chat is off, or there is no such conversation

409.description: Chat is on but its provider setting is unusable

429.description: Too many messages in the last minute; wait Retry-After seconds

502.description: The chat provider failed; the detail is redacted

post.summary: Send a message to the chat assistant

get.description:
The redacted `context` the next message would carry, and the opt-ins that shaped it.

Nothing is sent to a provider. Loopback only: a paired phone gets 403, because the context is
the user's agenda. Works while chat is off (`enabled` false), so the user can look before
opting in.

404.description: Chat is not wired into this server

409.description: Chat is on but its provider setting is unusable

get.description:
Up to 5 candidates (`name`, `region`, `country`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `population`).

Open-Meteo's order is kept and nothing is picked for the caller: the user chooses one and the
stored `latitude` and `longitude` are then set as usual. Loopback only: a paired phone gets
403. At most 10 searches a minute (429 with `Retry-After`). The query text is never logged.

429.description: Too many searches in the last minute; wait Retry-After seconds

502.description: Open-Meteo could not answer; the detail is redacted

get.description: Report that the server is up.

Items completed (by you, or seen done at the source) and items that disappeared, by day.

`from` and `to` are calendar days in the configured timezone, both included, at most 366 days
apart. Only days with something to show are returned, oldest first. Each entry carries
`completed_by` (`user`, `source`, or null for an item that disappeared), its source, title and
its note, if it has one. `reopened` is true for an item the source completed and later reported
open again; it stays on the day it was completed (decision 0130).

schema.title: Response Get Settings V1 Settings Get

delete.description:
Delete every stored key, event and sync state of the source.

Work already in flight for the source is cancelled first: whatever it reports afterwards is
dropped. A failure is a 200 with an "error" `sync`: nothing was removed (the cancel failed), or
the credentials are gone but some stored data is not ("incomplete"); disconnect again to finish.

put.description:
Validate and store the credentials; the sync starts after the response (state "syncing").

In distributed mode the api runs no sync: it queues a job for the source's worker, and
`GET /v1/settings` shows the state the normalizer records when the worker reports.

A credential-only integration (the Gemini key) has no sync: its result carries `sync` null.

With `unverified: true` the credentials are stored without validation and no sync follows;
a source is then left in an `error` state whose message starts with `Saved unverified:`.
A failed connect sets `can_save_unverified` only after a transient (network) error.

get.description:
The summary for `date`, with the `provider` it came from and whether it was `cached`.

404 when summaries are off (the default). A provider failure never fails the request: the
last stored summary (`provider` "stored") or a built-in one (`provider` "template") is returned.

post.description:
Sync all sources and return each one's new state; a failing source does not raise.

In distributed mode nothing is fetched here: a job is queued for every connected source and
each is returned as "syncing" (as "error" if its job could not be queued, say because Redis
is down; the others are still queued); the other sources are returned as last recorded.
Read the results from `GET /v1/settings` once the workers have reported.

schema.title: Response Sync All V1 Sync Post
